sector: Cross-border export logistics (Dongguan electronics/manufacturing cluster; ports, customs, multimodal freight)
hitl_conditions: Not discussed; the paper only contrasts system response times with manual processes and offers an interpretability module that visualises the agents' game for analysts; no approval, override or escalation conditions are described.
key_finding: MARL (Double Dueling DQN agents for manufacturers, logistics providers, ports, customs) trained in a digital-twin simulation of the Dongguan export corridor reportedly cuts cost/TEU 22% vs GA, raises deadline compliance to 94.2% and re-plans disruptions in 43 s; agents coordinate without centralised oversight. Reported figures are internally inconsistent.

quotes.text: As shown in Figure 1, the architecture builds a symbiotic relationship between a geo-aware MARL decision engine and a digital twin-enabled supply chain simulation platform, thus facilitating the evolutionary optimisation of cross-border logistics paths.
Digital Twin Environment Configuration.Geospatial resolution: 1km² per grid cell (150×150 grid).Dynamic event modeling:Port congestion: Modified Poisson process (λ=0.35 ± 0.12 during typhoon season).
quotes.section: 3.1.2 Experimental Validation (the 'twin' is a synthetic simulation environment: Poisson congestion, ARIMA fuel prices, Weibull customs delays)

quotes.text: we build a three-layer interactive model comprising manufacturers, logistics providers, and customs regulators, thereby overcoming the limitations of traditional static path planning.

Built on Mesa-ABM 1.2.3 and Ray RLlib 2.8.1, the multi-agent simulation environment implements a decentralized decision-making protocol. Each intelligent agent (n=387 in full-scale simulation) employs modified Double Dueling DQN architecture with prioritized experience replay

By linking each participant's rewards to global KPIs, including carbon emissions (down 14.2%), infrastructure utilisation (up 31%), and clearance times (down 27%), the model facilitates the formation of collaborative strategies without the need for centralised oversight.
quotes.section: 5 Conclusions (HITL: no human/central oversight in the loop)

quotes.text: Validation with electronics exporters in the Dongguan region (17 companies in total) confirms its practical feasibility [...] The average response time for emergency reprogramming was 22 minutes (compared to 6.3 hours for manual processes).
